findings.title: Per-user working-hours check rejects slots whenever a user has more than one working-hours entry for a day
findings.body:
`workingHours.find(...)` returns true, meaning the slot is rejected, as soon as any single entry covering that weekday does not contain the slot. It does not check whether at least one entry contains it.

Users routinely have several entries for the same day:
- Split availability, e.g. 9-12 and 13-17.
- Hours that cross UTC midnight, which `getWorkingHours` splits into two entries with shifted `days`. For example, US Pacific 9am-6pm becomes ~16:00-24:00 UTC plus 00:00-01:00 UTC.

A 14:00 slot is outside the 9-12 entry and gets rejected. Each Pacific-time slot is outside one of its two UTC fragments, so every slot is rejected.

This check now runs for every fixed host. For non-team event types every user is `isFixed`, so personal booking pages for these users lose most or all of their slots. The logic should require the slot to be inside at least one applicable range (`some`), not reject it if it is outside any one range.

findings.title: Busy times are skipped entirely on days with a date override
findings.body:
When a date override matches the slot's day and the slot is not rejected, `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` returns before the `busy.every(...)` check runs.

On any day with a date override, the user's existing Cal bookings, external calendar events and buffers are therefore ignored. Slots that overlap them are shown as available, for both fixed and round-robin hosts, inviting double bookings or failures at booking time.

The override and working-hours checks should only reject slots; slots that pass them should still go through the busy check.

findings.title: Multiple date-override ranges on the same day reject slots inside any range but the first
findings.body:
`dateOverrides.find(...)` returns true, so the slot is marked unavailable, as soon as one override on that day does not contain the slot. Cal.com lets a date override have several time ranges, e.g. 9-10 and 14-15.

A 14:00 slot is checked against the 9-10 override first. `slotStartTime.isAfter(end)` is true, so the slot is rejected even though it lies within the 14-15 range.

The check should reject a slot only if it falls inside none of that day's override ranges.

findings.title: Override day matching uses the UTC (or server-local) date instead of the organizer's local date
findings.body:
The override is matched to a slot by comparing `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset).format("YYYY MM DD")` with `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` in UTC. Two problems follow.

1. Wrong day for non-UTC organizers. An IST user marking Apr 17 unavailable (stored as 00:00-00:00) produces start = Apr 16 18:30Z. Slots on Apr 17 UTC, i.e. the fixed host's whole IST working day, never match the override and fall through to the working-hours check, so they are shown as bookable. That defeats the purpose of this PR for fixed hosts. In the other direction, a slot at Apr 17 20:00Z (Apr 18 01:30 IST) is compared against the Apr 17 override and wrongly rejected.

2. Server timezone dependence. The left side is formatted in the server's local timezone while the right side is UTC, so results change on servers not running in UTC.

Matching should compare the slot's date in the organizer's timezone with the override's organizer-local date.

findings.title: Slots that only partially overlap a date override are accepted
findings.body:
A slot is rejected only if it ends at or before the override start, or starts after the override end.

This lets through slots that straddle either boundary:
- With override 14:00-15:00 and a 60-minute event, a 14:30 slot ends at 15:30 but is accepted because its start is not after 15:00.
- A 13:30 slot that starts before the override is also accepted.

Bookings can therefore extend outside the host's overridden availability. The check should require `slotStart >= overrideStart && slotEnd <= overrideEnd`.

findings.title: Working-hours end check uses slot start time instead of slot end time
findings.body: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` is identical to `start`, so the slot's end is never checked. A slot that starts inside working hours but runs past the end of the working day is not rejected. This looks like a copy-paste error; it should use `slotEndTime`.

findings.title: Identity comparison of two dayjs objects is always false
findings.body:
`dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two freshly created object references, so it is never true. The intended "unavailable all day" (start == end) short-circuit never fires.

A slot starting exactly at the override instant then passes both later checks: its end is not before start, and its start is not after end. It is treated as inside the override and shown as available on a day marked unavailable. Use `isSame`/`valueOf()` comparison instead.

findings.title: Override-to-invitee timezone shift wraps across midnight and drops or misplaces override slots
findings.body:
Override start/end are shifted by `inviteeOffset - organizerOffset` and reduced to `hour()*60 + minute()`. That arithmetic wraps modulo 24h without moving the range to the adjacent invitee day.

For an IST organizer with an override of 06:00-18:00 and an invitee in New York (offset -9:30), start becomes 20:30 (1230 min) and end becomes 08:30 (510 min). `buildSlots` discards the range as start >= end. The organizer's regular working hours for that day were already removed, so the invitee sees no slots that day.

The `activeOverrides` day filter also compares the organizer-wall-clock `override.start` against invitee-day instants without the offset. Overrides near midnight can be applied to the wrong invitee day. The conversion needs to work on absolute instants and handle ranges that span two invitee days.

findings.title: New tests don't cover the round-robin fixed-host fix or the new checkIfIsAvailable logic
findings.body:
The only added test re-runs the single-user override scenario in another timezone. Nothing exercises the PR's main change: a round-robin event with a fixed host whose date override must constrain slots.

The following are also untested:
- Bookings or busy calendar time on a date-override day.
- Multi-range overrides.
- Working hours with split ranges or ranges crossing UTC midnight.
- "Unavailable" (00:00-00:00) overrides for a non-UTC host.

The existing IST 9:30-18:00 fixture maps to a single UTC range and a single override, so serious regressions in `checkIfIsAvailable` pass unnoticed: whole-day loss of slots, skipped busy times, and wrong day matching.
